subject: AWS Marketplace listing snippets + co-sell enablement sync
messages:
From: Heather Lang <heather.lang@atlascloud.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Chan <sarah.chan@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AWS listing copy + co-sell prep

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for taking this on. We’re ramping towards a Q4 launch for Atlas Cloud’s managed LLM suite and AWS Marketplace listing is a blocker for co-sell certification. Can you help with two things this week?

1) Short marketing snippets (1-liner, 30-word, 75-word) that map to the product page hero and bullets.
2) A short paragraph that explains our usage/pricing model with clear footnotes we can hand to Procurement and AWS field.

We’ve attached the technical overview from our side (PDF) and will need anything you produce to reference the correct AMI/entitlement names. Sarah — feel free to chime in on AWS expectations.

Appreciate it — Heather

(attachment: atlas_managed_llm_overview.pdf)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Heather Lang <heather.lang@atlascloud.com>
Cc: Sarah Chan <sarah.chan@amazon.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS listing copy + co-sell prep

Hi Heather —

We can do that. I’m attaching a first-pass doc with suggested hero snippets and three pricing-footnote options that align to AWS private offers and pay-as-you-go SKUs. High-level plan:

- Today: first-pass snippets + pricing footnote table (attached rwf_aws_listing_snippets_v1.docx, pricing-footnotes-table.csv)
- Tomorrow AM: internal copy review with Kimberly and Jonas to surface any compliance/language blockers
- Wed: updated copy for Atlas review and AWS field review

Quick questions to make the copy precise:
- Which entitlements should appear as the default SKU (managed-inference-v1 vs managed-inference-pro)?
- Any required compliance callouts for customer-facing page (SOC2 mention / regional data residency)?

I’ve cc’d Kimberly for legal/eligibility checks.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Partnerships (Marketplace)
Redwood Inference

(attachments: rwf_aws_listing_snippets_v1.docx, pricing-footnotes-table.csv)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-22T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: quick copy/legal pass on Atlas snippets

Soojin —

I reviewed the first-pass doc. High-level notes:
- Hero 1-liner is fine but tweak the claim about "enterprise-grade SLA" — need to avoid an SLA promise unless the customer signs a Dedicated contract. Suggest: "production-ready SLAs available".
- Pricing footnotes: good to call out metering granularity (vCPU-min vs token-equivalents). Atlas needs to pick a single metering unit for the listing to avoid buyer confusion.
- Add a short sentence on data handling: "Customer prompts and outputs are not used to train models" (only if Atlas agrees).

Jonas — can you double-check the AMI entitlement names in the attached playbook? I flagged potential mismatch on the managed-inference-pro SKU label.

Kimberly
General Counsel (Marketplace Compliance)
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-23T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: quick copy/legal pass on Atlas snippets

On Mon, Aug 23, 2027 at 08:07 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jonas — can you double-check the AMI entitlement names in the attached playbook?

I pulled the AMI registry and confirmed: the public AMI for Atlas "atlas-managed-llm-v1" is correct. The label "managed-inference-pro" in Atlas materials maps to our internal offering code "redwood-dedicated-v2" — that mismatch will confuse the AWS listing.

Recommendation: align to the Atlas AMI name for the customer-facing page and include an internal mapping table in the co-sell playbook (we added that to co-sell-playbook-atlas-annotated.pdf).

Also added a suggested 2-line buyer-facing usage example that clarifies burst vs committed capacity. See the updated PDF.

-Jonas
Senior Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Heather Lang <heather.lang@atlascloud.com>, Sarah Chan <sarah.chan@amazon.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-23T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: Updated listing snippets + annotated playbook (for Atlas review)

Heather — attaching an updated set based on internal review. Changes you’ll see:

- Hero 1-liner: "Managed LLM inference for product teams — predictable performance, simple entitlements." (keeps benefits, removes direct SLA claim)
- 30-word and 75-word variants included for hero and bullets.
- Pricing footnote options: Option A (PAYG token-equivalent metering), Option B (vCPU-minute metering), Option C (commit + burst). I recommend Option C for Atlas if you plan to offer reserved capacity to enterprise customers because it maps cleanly to AWS Private Offers.
- AMI / SKU names: public-facing listing will use "atlas-managed-llm-v1"; internal mapping present in the playbook PDF.
- Added buyer usage example for burst vs committed usage to reduce procurement questions.

Next steps: please confirm which pricing option Atlas prefers and whether you approve the data-handling sentence in bullet 4 of the product description. If approved we’ll push the updated copy to the Marketplace draft and loop AWS for co-sell enablement.

Thanks —
Soojin
(attachments: rwf_aws_listing_snippets_v1.docx, co-sell-playbook-atlas-annotated.pdf)

From: Heather Lang <heather.lang@atlascloud.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Chan <sarah.chan@amazon.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-24T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Updated listing snippets + annotated playbook (for Atlas review)

Soojin, team —

This is great, thank you. Quick answers:
- We will go with Option C (commit + burst) — procurement likes the predictability and it fits our channel discounts.
- Atlas confirms the public AMI name "atlas-managed-llm-v1"; we’ll accept the mapping table in the playbook.
- Data handling sentence is approved: "Customer prompts and outputs are not used to train models." Please include a short parenthetical about our ability to enable customer-managed encryption at rest (we have an HSM-backed KMS option).

Sarah — can you confirm AWS field readiness once we mark the listing draft ready? We’d like an intro to the co-sell enablement rep.

If everything looks good from your side, Soojin, please proceed to update the Marketplace draft and add HubSpot notes under DEAL-7321.

Best,
Heather Lang
VP, Partnerships — Atlas Cloud

(attachment: procurement_requirements.xlsx)
